title: Son Heung-min continues post-World Cup hot streak with MLS All-Star Game MVP
content:
One of the more bizarre stats from the opening portion of the MLS season was that Son Heung-min hadn’t scored a league goal. A world-renowned star who scored nine goals in his first 10 games after joining LAFC last summer led the league in assists but hadn’t managed to find his scoring form.

Coming out of a disappointing World Cup for South Korea, Son has flipped the switch and then some.

On the heels of three straight league games with a goal, Son was the brightest MLS All-Star of them all, scoring a pair in a 4-3 win over Liga MX’s All-Stars on Wednesday night in Charlotte, N.C., and taking home match MVP honors. He’s the second Korean player to win MLS All-Star MVP, the first since Park Ji-sung did it in 2011, when MLS’ best took on Manchester United in New Jersey.

New England Revolution star Carles Gil assisted both of Son’s strikes, three minutes apart, to power the MLS to the lead midway through the first half after Chivas center back Luis Gabriel Rey’s early opener for the Mexican league. MLS has won four of the five meetings between the leagues in an exhibition whose format has changed many times but has settled more frequently on this setup.

The Chicago Fire’s Philip Zinckernagel, who was a late addition after Lionel Messi, Rodrigo De Paul, Hugo Cuypers and Mbekezeli Mbokazi withdrew, scored MLS’ third, and FC Cincinnati’s Evander finished the scoring for MLS. Venezuelan veteran and Pachuca forward Salomón Rondón and Cruz Azul’s José Paradela scored Liga MX’s other goals. The result was preserved by Orlando City and Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau, who came on just past the hour mark and made six saves in that brief cameo.

But the star of the day was Son, who first scored from a close-range, left-sided angle in the 20th minute.

His second, in the 23rd, was far more picturesque, with Gil doing well to keep the ball in play before clipping a perfect ball into the center of the box, where an in-stride Son connected for the volley.

There’s little time for Son to celebrate the achievement, as a giant league fixture beckons in a few days. Son and Thomas Müller might have been joking around with each other as part of the prematch festivities, but they’ll go head to head Saturday as LAFC heads to Vancouver, B.C., where two of the three teams tied atop the Western Conference will meet.
